preserved_objections.basis: The claimed oxidation of silver nanowires in sweat environment directly contradicts the proposed mechanism's requirement for high electrical conductivity, as silver oxide formation would significantly increase electrical resistance and degrade sensor performance

The pH range of 4-8 specified in boundary conditions is insufficient for real-world sweat pH variations, which can range from 3.5 to 7.5, potentially causing MoS2 degradation at the lower end and affecting glucose oxidation active sites

The provided evidence [doi:10.1038/s41598-026-42857-6] specifically documents Ag nanowire oxidation in physiological environments, directly contradicting the candidate's claim of silver nanowire stability in sweat conditions

The candidate fails to demonstrate any quantitative advantage over current electrodes in protein resistance, with only a 40% reduction claim that doesn't address the fundamental encapsulation mechanism that affects all existing electrode materials

Hydrothermal synthesis of a stable silver nanowire/Ti3C2 MXene/MoS2 composite with consistent properties at nanoscale dimensions is technologically unfeasible with current manufacturing capabilities, as evidenced by the lack of commercial implementations of such complex 2D material composites

The testable prediction focuses solely on protein adhesion measured by quartz crystal microbalance but fails to account for the complex biological response including fibroblast adhesion and collagen deposition that actually causes signal attenuation in vivo
